messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing ~3% of quantized eval runs where per-sample trace objects are reported in the manifest but 404 on fetch. Happening on branch quant-2026-03 and affects both hosted + dedicated runs. Anyone else?
kevin: saw the same alert coming from eval-trace-missing-rule. spike started yesterday around 02:30 UTC. failing jobs list shows multipart uploads for traces > 5MB are the common factor.
sam: quick dump of uploader key code that might be the culprit:

```python
# uploader.py (simplified)
object_key = f"{bucket}/{prefix}/{run_id}/{sample_id}.json.gz"
# earlier we used quote_plus for the manifest entry, but the s3 client uses quote
manifest_key = urllib.parse.quote_plus(object_key)
s3_client.upload_fileobj(..., Key=urllib.parse.quote(object_key))
```

sam: TL;DR: manifest contains a different encoded key than the actual object because we accidentally mixed quote_plus vs quote. When sample_id contains chars like ':' or '+' or spaces the encoded strings diverge and the downloader looks at the manifest key and then does a straight get_object which 404s.
elaine: confirmed in logs: downloader trying to GET key with '+' where S3 object exists with '%3A' for ':' . ls shows:

$ aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-eval-traces --prefix quant-2026-03/
{"Contents": [{"Key": "quant-2026-03/run-721/abc%3A123.json.gz", ...}]}
# but manifest line had: quant-2026-03/run-721/abc+123.json.gz

kevin: ugh. Related thing: our retention GC job uses prefix matching that strips trailing slashes. If run_id collisions happen (run-72 vs run-721) and we build prefix like f"{bucket}/{prefix}/{run_id}" without a trailing slash, the GC's startswith check occasionally matches siblings and deletes older runs. I think two independent bugs compounded.
maria: repro steps I ran locally: 1) create sample id with colon and plus, 2) run uploader to generate manifest, 3) list objects in bucket -> object exists only under percent-encoded key, 4) downloader reads manifest and does get_object on the +-encoded key -> 404. Also ran the GC script in dry-run and saw matching results for run-72 when intended run-721.

sam: proposed fixes:
- stop encoding object_key in manifest: store the raw object_key (or store an explicit object_key field that is the exact Key used in S3).
- standardize encoding: use urllib.parse.quote with safe=''. one canonical path for both upload and manifest.
- GC fix: ensure prefix match includes trailing slash or use fullKey equality for exact run_id segments. add unit tests for run ids with partial collisions.

maria: patch outline I pushed to my fork:
```diff
- manifest_entry['s3_key'] = urllib.parse.quote_plus(object_key)
+ # store the exact key we uploaded so retrieval is 1:1
+ manifest_entry['s3_key'] = uploaded_key  # uploaded_key comes from the s3 client response:: Key
```
and in uploader we now do: uploaded_key = urllib.parse.quote(object_key, safe='')

kevin: added CI checks: new unit test test_special_char_sample_ids asserts that uploader->manifest->downloader roundtrip succeeds for sample ids: ["abc:123","a b","plus+sign","unicode-ß"]. Also added a tiny e2e in the qa pipeline that does an actual upload to the s3 staging bucket and verifies GET. CI job name: eval-trace-e2e-encoding.

elaine: I patched the gc script in place: require prefix to end with '/' before startswith, and added a regex check for exact run directory segment: re.compile(rf"/{re.escape(run_id)}/"). Dry-run showed no sibling deletions.

runner-bot: CI: eval-trace-e2e-encoding failed on fork (link: https://ci.example/redwood/1234) — failure was flaky permission error against staging bucket.
kevin: change made: use presigned PUT in the e2e to avoid IAM timing flakiness. retriggered.

maria: merged fix into quant-2026-03, created tracking issue #5421: "manifest uses canonical s3_key and GC prefix exact-match". Test plan in the issue: unit + e2e + monitor the prom rule for missing traces. Rolling patch to hosted runners tonight, Dedicated after smoke passes.
sam: follow-ups: 1) add a linter CI check to prevent mixing quote/quote_plus across modules, 2) surface object_key in the eval dashboard so support can download directly when manifest looks wrong, 3) consider base64-encoding sample ids for keys to avoid any ambiguity.

elaine: postmortem note: two separate low-sev bugs combined to cause the ~3% missing-trace rate: inconsistent encoding and a sloppy prefix match in GC. severity medium but operationally noisy. I'll add a short blameless summary to the incidents channel after we verify rollback metrics. :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks all — allocating a 1h blameless sync after the hosted rollout to verify the fix and check retention logs. If anyone wants to pair on the e2e flakiness please ping me. :coffee:
